repo:objectstack#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5oyZgRX9Qc1ZHsMRQp

An update to the description above. Since #34494 `b7751333` (contract review 6933112344 S3), the reading no longer digests the stored bodies. It digests `id`, `type`, `name`, `namespace`, `package_id`, `bundle_member`, `extends`, `strategy`, `state`, `version`, `checksum` and `updated_at`. The class this card exists to close is now narrower: a writer that bypasses the engine and rewrites a body while leaving `version`, `checksum` and `updated_at` exactly as they were. Today that class is bounded only by the compile cache's 10-bound age cap.

The same synthetic run on the bookkeeping-only reading took 0.3, 2.2 and 21 ms at 100, 1 000 and 10 000 rows. On a showcase store seeded with 5 000 rows, a renewed bundle reload took 150–192 ms with 42 queries, against a 491 ms recompile (delta 6933554702 on #34494). The column this card asks for would let the reading drop to one small value and close the bypass class without the cap.

## Triage: first touch → `domain:server` · p2 · theme: performance · 2026-11-17T00:47Z

⛔ Not a claim.

The compile cache confirms freshness every 30 s by hashing every `sys_metadata` row, bodies included, which reads the whole table. A write-moved column would make that check one indexed read. This is a performance follow-up of #34206, which the maintainer raised to p1: **p2**.
